title: Table rows with h="0" overlap each other; table is missing from PDF export
author: rclinux
body:
**Version:** deckcraft 0.3.0, Linux x86_64 release tarball (Arch-based distro, Wayland)

### What happens
A table on a slide renders with all of its rows drawn on top of each other at the same position. In my test, "1 alpha" and "2 beta" overlap into one unreadable line and the header row ("Col A / Col B") can't be seen. In `deckcraft-cli convert deck.pptx out.pdf` the table text is missing from the PDF entirely (`pdftotext` finds no table text).

Saving back to .pptx keeps the table: LibreOffice opens DeckCraft's re-saved file and shows the table correctly. So the problem looks like it's in layout and rendering, not in loading or saving.

### Probable cause
The table rows have a height of zero:

```xml
<a:tbl> ... <a:tr h="0"> ... </a:tr> <a:tr h="0"> ... </a:tr> <a:tr h="0"> ... </a:tr>
```

In PowerPoint, `a:tr/@h` is a minimum: each row grows to fit its text. DeckCraft appears to use it as an exact height, so every row is placed at y = 0 inside the table frame. pandoc writes `h="0"` for every table, and other generators (python-pptx, scripts) often do too.

### Steps to reproduce
```sh
printf '# Slide\n\n| Col A | Col B |\n|------:|-------|\n| 1 | alpha |\n| 2 | beta |\n' > t.md
pandoc t.md -t pptx -o t.pptx      # pandoc 3.10.2
deckcraft-cli render t.pptx out.png
deckcraft-cli convert t.pptx out.pdf
```

### Expected
Each row is at least tall enough for its text and rows stack vertically, as in PowerPoint and LibreOffice Impress.

title: Linux source build fails: alsa-lib-devel (libasound2-dev) needed but not documented
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Building DeckCraft from source on Linux fails unless the ALSA development headers are installed, and the README doesn't list this requirement.

**Environment:** Fedora 44 (Nobara), x86_64, rustc 1.98.1; deckcraft `main` @ baff6a2

**Steps:**
```sh
git clone https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft && cd deckcraft
cargo build --release -p deckcraft
```

**Result:**
```
error: failed to run custom build command for `alsa-sys v0.3.1`
```
`alsa-sys` comes in through `cpal = "0.16"` in `apps/deckcraft/Cargo.toml`. It needs `alsa.pc`, which pkg-config can't find without the -devel package.

**Fix:** `sudo dnf install alsa-lib-devel` (Debian/Ubuntu: `libasound2-dev`), then the build succeeds.

**Suggestion:** add a short "Building on Linux" note to the README's Quick start listing `alsa-lib-devel` / `libasound2-dev`. WordCraft, GridCraft and PdfCraft built on the same machine without it, so this is only needed for DeckCraft.

title: Linux (GNOME Wayland): window title bar doesn't match the desktop theme
author: fqazzazee
body:
## Environment

- Fedora 44, GNOME Shell 50.5, Wayland session, 167% display scaling
- Built from source at `4b09f35`

## Title bar doesn't follow the GNOME theme (Wayland)

On GNOME Wayland, the app draws its own title bar. This app shows winit's plain fallback bar, which
ignores the GNOME theme, dark mode and button layout.

The workspace sets `eframe = { version = "0.36", default-features = false }` (`Cargo.toml:66`),
which also drops winit's default `wayland-csd-adwaita` feature, so `sctk-adwaita` isn't in
`Cargo.lock`.

Possible fixes:

- Enable `winit/wayland-csd-adwaita`, so the title bar follows GNOME's look and light/dark mode, or
- Draw an in-app title bar, as PhotoCraft does on Linux.

Workaround: start the app through Xwayland (`env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY deckcraft`), so GNOME draws a real
title bar.

Same issue in GridCraft, with more detail: https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/54

title: Animated GIFs show only their first frame (no playback, no pause)
author: DimaSmaha
body:
## Problem

  An animated GIF inserted into a presentation, or imported with a PPTX, stays frozen on its first frame. It doesn't play in the editor or in the slide show, and there's no way to play or pause it.

  ## Steps to reproduce

  1. Run `cargo run --release -p deckcraft`.
  2. Insert an animated GIF (Insert ▸ Picture), or open a PPTX that contains one.
  3. Look at it in the editor, then start the slide show.

  **Expected:** the GIF plays (loops) in the editor and in the show, and you can pause and resume it, like PowerPoint's corner play/pause button.

  **Actual:** only the first frame is shown, in both views.

  ## Cause

  `crates/render/src/images.rs` decodes every picture with `image::load_from_memory(..).to_rgba8()`, which keeps only the first frame. The editor and the show then cache the rendered slide, and
  nothing redraws it over time.

  ## Proposed fix

  - Decode all GIF frames and draw the frame for each GIF's play time (exports keep the first frame).
  - Redraw only when a GIF reaches its next frame.
  - Add a play/pause button on hover, plus a `media.gifPlay` command so the CLI, control channel and MCP can do the same.

  ## Environment

  - Windows 11
  - DeckCraft 0.3.0 (`main` at 4b09f35)

title: Add a System theme option that follows the macOS light/dark appearance

body:
## Summary

Add a System choice to DeckCraft's interface theme setting that follows the macOS light/dark appearance live, so the app changes with the rest of the desktop when macOS switches appearance automatically.

## Problem to solve

macOS can switch between Light and Dark appearance automatically (System Settings → Appearance → Auto changes it at sunset and sunrise), and many Mac apps offer a "System" theme choice that tracks it.

DeckCraft offers only a manual light/dark switch. `Brightness` in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` has only `Light` (the default) and `Dark`, persisted as `brightness` in `ui.json`. title: Text in flipped shapes is drawn mirrored
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Text in a flipped shape is drawn mirrored. `flipH` mirrors the glyphs left to right, and `flipV` mirrors them upside down. A common case: the label on a "left arrow" made by flipping a right arrow reads backwards.

**Repro:** a slide with a `rightArrow` shape that has `<a:xfrm flipH="1">` and the text "Next" (python-pptx: add the shape, then set `flipH="1"` on its `a:xfrm`).

**Expected (PowerPoint):** flips mirror the geometry, never the text. `flipH` text stays upright and readable; `flipV` (or both flips) turns it 180°. The same applies inside flipped groups.

**Actual:** mirrored glyphs. Clicking the label also places the caret at the mirrored position, so a double-click selects the wrong characters.

**Cause:** `shape()` in `crates/render/src/lib.rs` draws text with the shape's full transform, flip scale included. The editing caret and hit-testing use the same transform.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, deckcraft `main` @ 4b09f35 (0.3.0).

Fix in #35.

title: Date fields are blank, or show another slide's fixed date text
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Automatic date fields (`<a:fld type="datetime1">`, `datetimeFigureOut`, …) show the deck-wide fixed date text instead of the date. On most decks they are blank. If any one slide has fixed date text in its date placeholder, every slide's date field shows that text.

**Repro:** a 4-slide deck whose footers use `datetime1`, `datetimeFigureOut`, a fixed text "Fixed date text" (plain text in that slide's date placeholder) and `datetime4`.

**Expected (PowerPoint):** the automatic fields show today's date in their type's format (e.g. 10/9/2026, October 9, 2026). The slide with fixed text shows its text.

**Actual:** all four slides show "Fixed date text". Without that slide, all four would be blank.

**Cause:** `SlideFields::field` (`crates/render/src/lib.rs`) returns `header_footer.date_text` for every `datetime*` field. The reader (`header_footer()` in `crates/pptx/src/read/mod.rs`) fills that from the first slide whose date placeholder has plain text.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, deckcraft `main` @ 4b09f35 (0.3.0).

Fix in #36.

title: feat(distribution): provide reliable CLI access with desktop packages
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Give desktop installations of DeckCraft a documented CLI invocation that people, scripts, and agents can use on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

## Problem to solve

Including a CLI executable in a package does not always make a shell command available. Windows installs the CLI beside the app; Linux native packages install it in `/usr/bin`, while AppImage and Flatpak keep it inside their package. macOS publishes a separate CLI download. Users need a supported invocation that matches their desktop installation without guessing its location or modifying global settings.

## Proposed behavior

Provide a callable CLI with each desktop distribution or an integrated installation route where needed, and document the exact invocation outside the agent setup UI. Preserve the existing CLI commands and MCP subcommand.

For Windows MSI, document full-path invocation of the installed CLI and make any shell exposure an explicit choice. Portable ZIP users can run its included executable without a global installation. For Linux DEB/RPM, preserve the existing `/usr/bin` CLI. Provide supported AppImage and Flatpak invocation through a wrapper or command override with the required arguments. - Linux tarball users can invoke the extracted CLI using the advertised path or optional installation procedure without building from source.

title: Feature request: AutoSave & version history to storage you own (local/NAS, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3/R2 via rclone), slide-level sharing, and no silent data loss on .pptx
author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR
PowerPoint's AutoSave, version history and co-authoring depend on OneDrive/SharePoint. Please add an open equivalent: a central "Save target" so a deck can autosave and keep versions on storage the user owns, with slide-level sharing later. Opt-in, no vendor server, no telemetry.

## Why (and why now)
- The README says unsaved work is kept by AutoRecover, which is a good base. This issue extends it to remote targets and versions.
- Related data-loss reports: #60 (Close silently discards an edited presentation), #105 (saving defaults to the *.deckcraft extension), and the PPTX round-trip losses in #70, #72, #74, #77 (comments, replies, audio/video options, animation rewind). A cloud autosave that silently replaces a .pptx with a lossy re-export would make these worse, so the proposal below is built around not doing that.

## How PowerPoint does it
- Microsoft documents co-authoring for PowerPoint, Word and OneNote on OneDrive and SharePoint. File > Save pushes your changes, pulls others' changes and updates version history on the server.
- AutoSave applies only to files on OneDrive/SharePoint; the first edit creates a version, then roughly one every 10 minutes. Otherwise only AutoRecover.
- The server merges; clients only negotiate locks and show a merge prompt when automatic merge fails.

## What DeckCraft has today (README only)
Native `.deckcraft`, .pptx open/save, AutoRecover, comments, sections, notes, embedded audio/video, 200+ commands (CLI/control channel/MCP), web build.

## Proposal
**Phase 0:** make AutoRecover a real write-ahead journal (atomic writes, recovery prompt, `file.autoSave` command). Fix the "close without asking" path (#60) first; it outranks this feature.
**Phase 1, Save target** (shared building blocks below). **Autosave writes the lossless native `.deckcraft` working copy to the target;** `.pptx` is written on explicit Save/Export, or via an opt-in "keep .pptx in sync" that warns about known lossy features. Keep the original .pptx …

title: Window decorations and title bar inconsistent with VectorCraft / PhotoCraft
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Description
The window decorations and title bar handling in `deckcraft` are inconsistent with the standard established in VectorCraft (PR #969) and PhotoCraft (PR #1903).

### Current Behavior
- On Windows and Linux, the application either does not draw client-side decorations/caption buttons or lacks consistent custom title bar handling.
- There is no option for users to toggle `System Title Bar` (native OS window decorations) in Preferences/User Interface.

### Desired Behavior
Standardize title bar and window decoration architecture to match VectorCraft:
1. Support custom client-side titlebar and window caption buttons (Minimize, Maximize/Restore, Close) with edge resize zones.
2. Provide a `System Title Bar` preference under User Interface to allow users to switch back to native OS decorations on Windows/Linux if desired.
3. macOS retains native window buttons and fullsize content view.

title: Feature (Beyond PPT) - Copy/Paste/Reference element
author: gNovp
body:
When working on huge PPTs, we sometimes need to have the exact same elements on multiple slides (like a text field with a number, quote, date... or an image for instance).

This can today be easily done with copy/pasting, but the copies are then unlinked (which makes it challenging when that specific content needs to be updated quickly before a presentation). Of course, the Slide Master solves a part of this issue, but it's far from ideal.

What if we had a new entry in the rightclick menu: Paste as Reference.
This button would link the elements together, meaning that an edit on any of these would instantly reflect on all the instanced copies.

This could apply to any element: text fields, images/icons, shapes, media, and could be a huge time saver (especially in huge presentations).
Of course, this feature could be specific to the .deckcraft file format (and copies unlinked if saving as .pptx, as it could be tricky to implement here, even if technically speaking, media in current PPTX files are already instances from ppt/media folder)

title: Feature (Beyond PPT) - Imported objects library
author: gNovp
body:
Following #122 , lots of times we need to reference an already imported media (video, image, sound, icon) into an other slide.
The way to do so today is to scroll in all the current slides, find the object, copy it, and paste it on the new slide.

It could be great to add a new side panel to DeckCraft, listing all the already imported objects (video, images, sounds, icons...) into the current slide deck, ideally presented via thumbnails. Then when clicking on one object of that list, having the option to just add it to the current slide, or add a reference to that object (allowing edits like in #122 ) would be a great time saver.

title: Feature (Beyond PPT) - Mark an object as Favorite
author: gNovp
body:

But as described in #123 , it can be tricky to go back and forward between slides to find this kind of object, and paste it, etc.

Building on the Library feature from #123 , it could be great to add to the context menu of selected objects (groups, or single elements like text fields, media etc) a "Favorite" entry. Once clicked, this object would be displayed on top of the the Library panel (from #123 ), to allow quick access and integration.

body:

Of course, Morph transitions can be used to workaround this issue (duplicating the slide, and repositionning the object). But in lots of cases it could be great to just be able to scroll an element (text, image, or even group) in place.

A list control could be added in the "Shape Format" tab, right under the size controls (Height and Width), with 4 choices:
- No scrolling
- Scroll horizontally
- Scroll vertically
- Scroll horizontally and vertically

author: gNovp
body:

But for more professional work, it's lacking.

When the video recording feature will be worked on for DeckCraft, it could be great to ask first to the user the mode of recording:
- Capture and embed (the current mode in Powerpoint, integrating the webcam video as an object in each slide)
- Capture for editing

The latter mode would still record the webcam, audio and timings, but it could place the files after the recording in the same folder as the presentation file itself. Thus, after the recording session, the user would then get: the presentation .deckcraft or .pptx file, a _webcam.mp4_ file and a _slideshow.mp4_ file.

And as a bonus, a precut FilmCraft project file embedding these files could also be placed here (or more generally a XML or CSV editlist that could be imported into any Video editing app). This would help tie in the apps in the Craft open ecosystem.

title: Feature (Beyond PPT) - Actions panel
author: gNovp
body:
Currently, PowerPoint and DeckCraft support interaction through hyperlinks placed on objects (via the "Link" context menu entry).

But on more complex presentations (with lots of references to external sources, or links to other slides etc), it can be difficult to work with that, as there is no place showing all links on a given slide.

It could be great to add a new Panel to DeckCraft (similar to the Animation pane, or Selection pane etc): the Action pane.
Displayed on the side of the current slide, it would allow to review all interactive elements in the current slide, set up if they would be triggered by click, keypress, or timer, etc...The pane could be divided into 3 parts:

- Actions on slide arrival
_Triggered when entering the current slide_

- Actions during the slide is displayed
_This section would show all objects having hyperlinks to external elements (URLs, files, etc), and links to other slides_

- Actions when leaving the slide

title: [Bug] macOS: double-clicking a .pptx in Finder shows "DeckCraft cannot open files in the Office Open XML presentation format"
author: SommerEngineering
body:
I made DeckCraft the default app for `.pptx` files on macOS. Double-clicking a `.pptx` in Finder
launches DeckCraft, but instead of the presentation, macOS shows this alert:

> The document “NAME.pptx” could not be opened. DeckCraft cannot open files in the “Office Open XML presentation” format.

Dragging the same file into the DeckCraft window opens it without problems, so the file itself is fine.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make DeckCraft the default app for `.pptx` files in Finder.
2. Double-click a `.pptx` file in Finder.

### Expected

DeckCraft opens the presentation.

### Actual

DeckCraft starts and shows the alert above. No presentation opens.

### Likely cause

The `Info.plist` of the v0.5.0 bundle has no `CFBundleDocumentTypes`, and winit 0.30 doesn't handle
the `kAEOpenDocuments` Apple event that Finder sends. AppKit then handles the event itself, finds no
document class for the type, and shows the alert. Drag & drop goes through winit, which is why it works.

#68 looks like it fixes exactly this: it adds the document types and a `kAEOpenDocuments` handler.

### Environment

- DeckCraft 0.5.0 (build a98df49b)
- macOS 27.0.1, Apple silicon

title: Arabic Language Support and Comprehensive Right-to-Left (RTL) Presentation Workflows
author: Wyetgf
body:
### Overview

If DeckCraft aims to become a complete open-source replacement for Microsoft PowerPoint, Arabic support should be treated as a first-class architectural and usability requirement—not merely as a translation of menus or the ability to display Arabic characters.

A reliable Arabic presentation workflow requires coordinated support across the user interface, text layout engine, slide model, editing tools, visual objects, charts, tables, animations, notes, import/export, accessibility, and automated testing.

The goal is not only to make Arabic text appear correctly. The application should ensure that Arabic and mixed Arabic–Latin content can be created, edited, formatted, presented, imported, exported, and reopened without unexpected changes in direction, ordering, alignment, positioning, or interaction behavior.

This request intentionally separates the requirements into specific functional areas. These are not repetitions of the same requirement: correct RTL interface mirroring, bidirectional text layout, cursor movement, chart labels, object positioning, animation direction, and file round-tripping are separate technical problems that can fail independently.

### 1. Fully mirrored RTL user interface

When Arabic is selected as the application language, DeckCraft should provide a complete RTL interface.

This should include:

- Mirroring of the main application layout, including sidebars, slide thumbnails, inspectors, navigation panels, dialogs, menus, and contextual menus.
- RTL-aware placement of toolbars, formatting controls, property panels, and presentation-management views.
- Correct ordering and alignment of buttons, tabs, breadcrumbs, dropdowns, toggles, checkboxes, radio buttons, and segmented controls.
- RTL-aware slide navigation and thumbnail presentation.
- Proper alignment of icons and labels without incorrectly mirroring icons whose meaning is not directional.
- Correct behavior for directional icons such as arrows, indentation controls, …

title: Chart render: automatic title (autoTitleDeleted=0, single series) is not drawn
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

`deckcraft-cli render` draws no title on a single-series chart that has `<c:autoTitleDeleted val="0"/>` and no explicit `<c:title>`. PowerPoint and LibreOffice both show an automatic title made from the series name (`Sales`). Charts made by python-pptx and other generators often rely on this auto title, so in deckcraft they silently lose their heading.

**Actual (deckcraft):** no title above the plot area.
**Expected (PowerPoint, LibreOffice):** the bold title `Sales` centred above the plot.

## Steps to reproduce

A single-series clustered column chart made with python-pptx 1.0.2 (`uv run --with python-pptx make.py`):

```python
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
from pptx.util import Inches

prs = Presentation()
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
data = CategoryChartData()
data.categories = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma"]
data.add_series("Sales", (42.1, 18.7, 6.3))
slide.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED, Inches(1), Inches(1), Inches(8), Inches(5.5), data)
prs.save("chart-single-series.pptx")
```

```
deckcraft-cli render chart-single-series.pptx --all out/
```

Reference: the same file exported to PDF by Microsoft PowerPoint for Mac (via AppleScript `save … as save as PDF`).

The chart XML has `<c:autoTitleDeleted val="0"/>`, no `<c:title>`, no `<c:varyColors>` element, and no `<c:max>`/`<c:majorUnit>` on the value axis.

## Environment

- deckcraft-cli 0.5.0 (also seen on 0.4.0), `deckcraft-cli-0.5.0-macos-universal.zip` from the release
- macOS 15.8.2, Intel x86_64
- Reference renderer: Microsoft PowerPoint for Mac. LibreOffice 26.8 matches PowerPoint on the title and the axis.

title: [Windows] 0.5.0 exits at startup: DXC runtime (dxcompiler.dll + dxil.dll) not shipped -> "Parent device is lost"
author: engmgs
body:
**deckcraft 0.5.0 (portable x64 zip and MSI, 2026-10-07 release) exits ~0.1 s after the window appears (exit code 1)** on Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26100, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (driver 32.0.16.1088), DirectX 12 default backend.

Same root cause as storytold/craft-launcher#126 (opened the same day) and storytold/lightcraft#471 (fixed there by #484). Of the twelve Craft apps installed on this machine the same log appears in cadcraft 0.5.0, wordcraft 0.5.0, gridcraft 0.5.0, soundcraft 0.5.0, vectorcraft 0.9.0; photocraft, filmcraft, lightcraft, pdfcraft, effectcraft and designcraft tolerate it.

**Log** (`%APPDATA%\DeckCraft\logs\deckcraft.log`, identical every start):
```
ERROR [main] wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("DXC compile error: warning: DXIL signing library (dxil.dll,libdxil.so) not found.  Resulting DXIL will not be signed for use in release environments.\r\n\n"))
WARN  [main] gpu_allocator::allocator::free_list_allocator: leak detected: { ... (wgpu internal) zero init buffer ... }
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
Error: Wgpu(RequestDeviceError(RequestDeviceError { inner: Core(Device(Lost)) }))
```

**Cause**: the build uses DXC for DX12 shader compilation (the wgpu `indirect_validation` compute pipeline) but ships neither `dxcompiler.dll` nor `dxil.dll`. The unsigned-DXIL warning is treated as a compile error, the pipeline fails, and the device is lost before the first frame.

**What I verified**
1. `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan` -> starts (as the cadcraft README troubleshooting section says).
2. A **matched** `dxcompiler.dll` + `dxil.dll` pair next to `<app>.exe` -> starts on DX12 from a plain double-click, no env var. Pair used: the one shipped with Microsoft Edge 154.0.4258.62.
3. `dxil.dll` alone (Chrome 154's copy) is **not** enough: `DXC compile error: error: validation errors / DXIL container mismatch for 'PSVRuntimeInfoSize' between 'PSV0' part:('48') …
